claim_text: R2 makes two §3.1 (formally-closed) accountability complements explicit, reuse-first, code-only (zero DATA INAMOVIBLE mutation; re-ingest stays human-gated). (1) ADMISSIBILITY PREDICATE: verify_output.admissible() returns H(c) in {0,1} as an EXTENSIBLE conjunction of hard invariants (v1 base: every external ENSDARG resolves). It makes the theorem explicit in code — admissibility is computed from hard predicates ONLY, never from a confidence/quality value — so no soft score can rescue an inadmissible claim (g(Q(c)) cannot flip H 0->1); soft scoring is defined only on H^{-1}(1). A VerificationReport.admissible property exposes the identifier component. (2) BAYES-PURITY verified_tier_weight: tier_weight() maps RAW=1.0 / DERIVED=0.7 / NOT_FOUND|unknown=0.0, DERIVED from the existing verification_tier (no manifest-schema change); ingest.py stamps it on the :Entity node and the :Document-[:MENTIONS]->:Entity edge at the human-gated ingest. Ledger purity = s*p/(s*p+f*(1-p)) contracts to 1 only on the deterministic subclass where f->0 (RAW). (3) info_priority_order is an HONEST EVPI PLACEHOLDER (NOT_FOUND->high info before verified; tagged placeholder:True); a calibrated EVPI needs a decision-utility model and is deferred. Verified offline NO-SPEND: the wt1a fabrication -> admissible=False; the correct ID -> admissible=True; tier weights 1.0/0.7/0.0; info_priority puts NOT_FOUND(clcnkb) before verified(wt1a); both files compile under -W error::DeprecationWarning; ingest.py NOT run (human-gated DI mutation).
